checks.notes: Measurement model (kinematics.ts): every star measured with Gaia DR3's precision for Gliese 445 (radial velocity 0.15 km/s; parallax distance error growing with distance squared), aimed along the alien's line of sight; the craft's own state is exact. A model, labelled as one.

checks.claim: Forty-four thousand years on, the alien's own fit of the map still points to a region that contains the Sun.
checks.measured: elapsed 44176 yr; centre (3.6, 3.1) pc, 95% semi-axes 14.5 x 6.5 pc (major axis toward l = 49 deg), sigma_theta 1.00 deg, rms 0.98 deg (alien frame, origin = Gliese 445 at the map epoch); Sun at (2.5, -3.3) pc, at the 72% contour; Gliese 445's own map-epoch position inside the region (at the 29% contour); 919 catalogued stars within 30 pc of the Sun inside. Without lengths: centre (3.5, 3.0) pc, 95% semi-axes 14.9 x 6.4 pc (major axis toward l = 49 deg), sigma_theta 1.00 deg, rms 0.99 deg
checks.expected: the Sun; Sagan's design claim about 20 pc (cover.md section 3)
checks.tolerance: Sun inside the 95% region
checks.notes: Gliese 445 was 5.27 pc from the Sun at the map epoch, so the region cannot tell the two apart if it is larger than that.

checks.claim: Reading the map as if seen from the other side of the galaxy (mirrored) makes the lines refuse to meet.
checks.measured: rms 94.97 deg mirrored vs 0.98 deg correct (ratio 96.6)
checks.expected: mirror ambiguity resolved by the fit (SSD72: it resolves once one pulsar is identified)
checks.tolerance: mirrored rms at least 5 times the correct one (spec)

checks.claim: The map's 14 directions, fitted onto today's pulsar positions, point back to a small region of the galactic plane that contains the Sun.
checks.measured: with lengths: centre (0.8, 6.3) pc, 95% semi-axes 15.0 x 6.7 pc (major axis toward l = 49 deg), sigma_theta 1.00 deg, rms 0.98 deg; Sun at the 69% contour; 982 catalogued stars within 30 pc fall inside it. Without lengths: centre (0.7, 6.2) pc, 95% semi-axes 14.7 x 6.7 pc (major axis toward l = 50 deg), sigma_theta 1.00 deg, rms 0.98 deg
checks.expected: the Sun (origin of the SSB frame); Sagan's design claim about 20 pc, '1 in 10^3 stars' (cover.md section 3)
checks.tolerance: Sun inside the 95% region (Monte Carlo over angle noise and distances, 2,000 draws)
checks.notes: Star count is a lower bound: HYG within 30 pc is incomplete for faint stars, and the region may extend beyond 30 pc.

checks.claim: Swapping the two nearest pulsars makes the map fit visibly poor, so a wrong match shows.
checks.measured: rms 49.13 deg swapped vs 0.98 deg correct (ratio 50.0); largest residual 172.1 deg
checks.expected: residuals far above the map's 3 deg accuracy
checks.tolerance: rms at least 3 times the correct fit (spec)
